title: Spurious Correlation-Aware Embedding Regularization for Worst-Group Robustness
claim: Decomposing group-mean embeddings into spurious and core components lets two regularizing losses suppress shortcut features and strengthen label-relevant ones.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: model stack, stacked group cards with loss boxes, ERM vs ours
description: The figure has three parts. On the left, a vertical stack of Feature Extractor, Embedding Space and Classifier runs down to Output. Colored MNIST-style digits (red or green 0s) feed in at the top. The wide middle panel zooms into the embedding space. It shows stacked cards, one per label-domain group (y, domain). Each card holds embedding vectors that are averaged into group means such as μ^{0,R} and μ^{1,G}. Minus circles pass the differences into a pink Spurious Feature box and a green Core Feature box. Along the bottom, magnitude and weight-alignment boxes are multiplied to give Spurious Loss (down arrow) and Core Loss (up arrow). The right panel compares ERM and SCER representation scatter plots of green and red digit tiles. The ERM plot clusters by color. The SCER plot clusters by digit label.
caption: Overview of the Spurious Correlation-Aware Embedding Regularization (SCER) framework. Input data is encoded into embeddings, from which group-wise mean embeddings are computed for each label-domain pair. SCER decomposes these into Spurious Features, capturing domain differences within each class, and Core Features, capturing class differences within each domain. Spurious Magnitude and Core Magnitude quantify the strength of domain-driven and label-driven variations. Weight-Spurious Alignment and Weight-Core Alignment measure how strongly the classifier aligns with each component. SCER constructs Spurious Loss and Core Loss from these terms to regulate the embedding space, reducing Spurious Loss to suppress domain-specific patterns while increasing Core Loss to reinforce label-relevant signals, thereby improving robustness to domain bias.
abstract: Deep learning models achieve strong performance across various domains but often rely on spurious correlations, making them vulnerable to distribution shifts. This issue is particularly severe in subpopulation shift scenarios, where models struggle in underrepresented groups. While existing methods have made progress in mitigating this issue, their performance gains are still constrained. They lack a rigorous theoretical framework connecting the embedding space representations with worst-group error. To address this limitation, we propose Spurious Correlation-Aware Embedding Regularization for Worst-Group Robustness (SCER), a novel approach that directly regularizes feature representations to suppress spurious cues. We show theoretically that worst-group error is influenced by how strongly the classifier relies on spurious versus core directions, identified from differences in group-wise mean embeddings across domains and classes. By imposing theoretical constraints at the embedding level, SCER encourages models to focus on core features while reducing sensitivity to spurious patterns. Through systematic evaluation on multiple vision and language, we show that SCER outperforms prior state-of-the-art studies in worst-group accuracy. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/MLAI-Yonsei/SCER}{https://github.com/MLAI-Yonsei/SCER}.
